extracted.intended_audience: research authors preparing journal rebuttal letters / manuscript revisions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing structured, professional rebuttal letters and associated manuscript revisions in response to peer reviewer comments to increase chances of journal acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Each response will provide references to revised analyses, tables and/or more recent literature (as relevant) in support of your position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the exact analyses/tables that were updated; point to empirical or literature evidence that justifies the response. Use precise, evidence-backed language rather than vague claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a respectful manner promotes collaboration; despite disagreement with reviewer opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt neutral, appreciative language; avoid emotional or defensive phrasing. Demonstrating professionalism builds editorial confidence and preserves relationships with reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a point-by-point list promotes transparency as well as increases editing management efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to each reviewer comment clearly and separately (point-by-point). Make it easy for editors/reviewers to verify corrections by referencing exact locations in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors prioritize clarity, completeness, and responsiveness over length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise but thorough rebuttal often outweighs extensive revisions without explanation. Focus on being complete and clear rather than verbose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize High-Impact Points
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize responses by theme, focusing on high-impact, 'deal-breaker' points rather than minor details, while maintaining a respectful tone to maximize persuasiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which critiques most affect acceptance and address those first. Avoid spending disproportionate effort on trivial comments at the expense of major concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Comments by Category
rubrics_metrics.description: Group the reviewer comments based upon their categorization (major, minor, technical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use categories to manage workload and to present a logical rebuttal structure; treat major issues with priority and more detailed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify Action for Each Comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a specific action (for example revision, justification, or clarification) for each comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For every reviewer point state whether you revised the manuscript, justified an existing approach, or clarified wording; be explicit about what was done and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Manuscript Changes Before Writing Rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Make any changes to the manuscript before writing the rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update the manuscript first so you can cite exact line and page numbers in the rebuttal; this shows edits are complete and helps reviewers verify changes quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Locations of Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the line and page numbers of all changes made to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise references (page/line or figure/table identifiers) for each stated change to enable quick verification by reviewers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check Tone, Consistency, and Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the rebuttal for its tone, consistency, and completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread for a neutral professional tone, ensure responses do not contradict one another, and confirm every reviewer comment is addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Methodology Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reviewer finds the methodology unclear: add schematic, provide citations for justification of design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include diagrams/schematics, detailed methodological descriptions, and citations that justify methodological choices. Clarify any steps that were ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Sample Size Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If sample size is questioned: provide power analysis or acknowledge as a limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible supply power/sample-size calculations; if not feasible, explicitly state and discuss the limitation and its implications for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Novelty Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If novelty is questioned: strengthen your discussion and provide additional comparative literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add literature comparisons, emphasize unique contributions, and revise the discussion/introduction to better situate the work relative to prior studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Language/Presentation Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers flag language issues: provide professional language editing acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional editing services if needed and state in the rebuttal that language/formatting issues have been corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage Disagreement Constructively
rubrics_metrics.description: If warranted by evidence, one may disagree with a reviewer without being dismissive. Authors should: recognise the viewpoint of the reviewer; support your disagreement with data; propose to revise or clarify in part when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the reviewer’s concern, present supporting data or rationale, and offer partial revisions or clarifications where feasible. Example phrasing: 'We appreciate the reviewer’s concern... While additional stratification was not feasible due to sample size, we have clarified this limitation and cited comparable approaches.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do: Use Neutral, Appreciative Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use neutral, appreciative language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start responses with appreciation phrases, avoid confrontational wording, and frame corrections as improvements made in response to constructive feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't: Use Emotional or Defensive Phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use emotional or defensive phrasing (DON'T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rebuttal language that attacks reviewers or minimizes their points. Defensive tone can harm persuasiveness and editorial perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do: Reference Revised Sections Clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference revised sections clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly point to the revised text, figures, or tables (with location identifiers) so reviewers can easily find and evaluate the changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't: Assume Reviewers Will Search for Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume reviewers will search for changes (DON'T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect reviewers to hunt through the manuscript; make changes easy to locate by giving precise citations and a clear point-by-point mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do: Address Every Comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Address every comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even for minor or tangential remarks, provide a brief response (e.g., 'addressed,' 'noted,' or reason for not changing) so editors see comprehensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't: Skip or Merge Unrelated Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Skip or merge unrelated comments (DON'T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid combining distinct reviewer points into a single response or omitting comments; this can appear evasive and reduce clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey Professionalism to Editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey professionalism to editors involved in making a final decision regarding the acceptance of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polished, well-documented, and respectful rebuttals signal the authors' editorial judgment and can influence editorial decisions positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Rebuttal as Strategic Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Think of your rebuttal as part of a strategic discussion with the scientific community rather than a simple response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured planning, courteous communication and evidence-based revisions to strengthen the manuscript and potentially convert reviewers into advocates.
